newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on short covering, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on short covering, soybeans.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher in a light-volume session on a combination of short covering, CBOT soybean spillover, mill pricing and concerns about seeding delays, traders said.
But a late bout of local profit taking bruised the rally and forced wheat to close off its session highs.

"Strength in other markets buoyed wheat, and technically we're still in an oversold situation," a KCBT trader said. "Everybody continues to be surprised, but the market appears not ready to go down yet. Wheat traders are (unwilling) to put on new short positions at these lower flat prices."
Traders said there was also support from fears that recent rains in the central Plains had disrupted HRW wheat planting.
KCBT wheat closed 2-1/4 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 2-1/4 cents but off the daily high of $4.33-1/2.

CIS was a leading buyer, having picked up at least two million July bushels and 1.7 million Dec. But CIS turned a seller and sold one million Dec. Traders said Dreyfus' Term Commodities bought 1.8 million March and sold two million July.
KCBT estimated Friday's wheat futures volume at 19.795 million bushels, down from Thursday's volume of 28.425.
